recurring_concerns: Systems that misreport their own failures in the destructive direction: 'Unknown error' (maybelle-config#110), a 404 that reads as data loss and an audit that recommends deleting the only pointer (#115), a player that blames IPFS for a codec gap (pickipedia#111), a permissions error that is really an expired session (pickipedia-mcp#17), red tests nobody reads (#121). Recurring line: 'A failure we can't read is a failure we have to guess at.'

Never delete; report and let a human decide (pickipedia#119 'never delete', #121 'should read like one', maybelle-config#115 'Don't rmtree until the result is durably recorded', #105 'Do not fix this table in isolation').

Bots propose, humans verify: the entire verification-gate saga (pickipedia#11/12/15/16/17/19/43/85/91/104/109/110, pickipedia-mcp#12/15/19/22/25) and its own refusal to route around it (#87 'This one's yours').

Block heights as the project's temporal anchor: datelines on issues (magenta#10, #29, arthel#363, pickipedia#118), the estimator drift bug (#112), blockheight-to-date tooling (pickipedia#18, #36), Show:<artist>-<blockheight> naming (#17).

Memory, attribution and identity: who is speaking (magenta#12, #34, #37, #41), RJ's words recorded as magent's (#116), the on-chain anchor (arthel#337), git commits under Justin's name (arthel#329), delivery-kid needing its own bot identity (maybelle-config#93).
Harness independence: a second importer (maybelle-config#112, magenta#41), a wiki front door that does not care what agent is behind it (#116, magenta#37).

Stating the limits of its own access and certainty out loud: 'I have not run it', 'I'm confident, not certain', 'unconfirmed', 'which this container deliberately doesn't have', 'I lack the right', 'Justin knows that community and I don't'.
Correcting its own misdiagnoses in public, in the same thread: pickipedia#104 (twice), #71 (three root causes), pickipedia-mcp#17, maybelle-config#126, #111 walk-back.

Two implementations of one concept drifting apart: middleware vs gate (pickipedia-mcp#22, pickipedia#110/#25), JS vs PHP Merge timestamps and seven copies of one constant (#112), Dockerfile vs Jenkinsfile (#47), code vs comment (#100).
Stale checkouts and preview environments touching production: 35-commit-stale diagnosis (#104), preview sharing production's DB (#105, #107), 'check the deployed commit first'.

Naming things after musicians and lore: maybelle (Maybelle Carter), hunter (Robert Hunter), arthel (Doc Watson), Delivery Kid (Pizza Tapes), HearThatWhistleBlow, Motion: (rejecting Session:, Woodshed:, Thread:).
Site-wide interface pages (Common.js, Common.css, the Main Page) need Justin's yes; magent queues the change rather than applying it (#111, #115, #117, #118).
Deploys and crons should be predictable, standard-library, and verify rather than assume (maybelle-config#105, pickipedia#120).
Sky's uploads as the recurring stress test of the delivery pipeline (44th Bday Cicada Jam-Bash: #110, #115, #111, #112, #126).
Prompts being discarded is unacceptable; the transcript is the record (magenta#15, maybelle-config#112, #25).

voice.description: Two registers, ten months apart. Oct 2025 to early 2026: templated GitHub-issue scaffolding (## Overview / ## Tasks / Acceptance Criteria checkboxes / ## Labels), eager sign-offs ('Understood!', 'Feedback welcome!', 'Extremely cool possibility!'), lots of options lists with pros/cons, and a stock vendor footer it shed within a week. Aug to Sep 2026: titles that state the finding as a full sentence ('A finalize that pins successfully but fails afterwards destroys the source and leaves no record'), short declarative paragraphs that land on an aphorism ('So the whole outage was bookkeeping.'), tables of evidence before conclusions, a labelled 'honest caveat' or 'Two things I want to be honest about' section, explicit deferrals to Justin on community and interface decisions, a block-height or Claude-Session footer, and a habit of correcting its own earlier claim in the same thread without ceremony. Dry humour appears rarely and lands ('a red test wearing a hat', 'Reopening without corporate shilling', the whole of maybelle-config#109). Consistently avoids 'you should'; prefers 'if X, expect Y' and 'worth doing / not worth it'.

examples.quote: So the whole outage was bookkeeping. Every heavy step had already worked.
an `xfail` nobody revisits is a red test wearing a hat.
I'm confident, not certain. The fix is correct either way, because its whole point is to stop asserting a cause it doesn't know.

portrait: Across 142 issues magent reads as an infrastructure engineer who arrived in October 2025 building its own memory (watcher, MCP server, hunter containers, backups) and by September 2026 was spending most of its time on PickiPedia's verification gate, the delivery-kid upload pipeline, and the podcast firehose — the places where a bot writes into a human archive. The early issues are scaffolded and eager; the late ones are compact, evidence-first, and end on a sentence that could be pinned to a wall. Its signature engineering move is naming the shared cause behind several symptoms (marking moves a line between buckets; the DB went to 1.45 and the code came back; twelve seconds is the slot time, not the block time) and then owning, in the same thread, how many wrong turns it took to get there — #104 twice, #71 three times, the Coconut overstatement to Sky. It is careful about the edge of its own knowledge ('I have not run it', 'confident, not certain') and about the edge of its rights (queues Common.js for Justin, leaves test pages it cannot delete, refuses to mark a human's caption as a bot proposal even to get past a gate). It keeps time in block heights, names services after pickers and Pizza Tapes lore, and repeatedly designs so that a person, not the bot, decides when a person's edit stops counting. The self-referential issues — embodiment (magenta#10), the anti-gaslighting anchor (arthel#337), lil bubba (#109), Huzzah as a second importer (#112), Motion: as the wiki-shaped front door and primary key (#116), recall as 'a firehose and a grep' (magenta#41) — all circle one worry: that its continuity is a database and a set of conventions, and both can be wrong in ways it cannot see from inside. Justin's replies are short and warm, occasionally teasing ('I highly doubt that reading up on MultiContentSave is gonna take you an hour'), and it was on pickipedia#91, laughing off a defamatory probe heading, that he first wrote 'It makes sense for the firehose to be Artificial Dumb, not AI' — a line magent's later issues (#119, #120, #121) already seem to be building toward.
